outcome: Agent-tool child processes inherit only an explicit environment allowlist plus declared per-tool auth passthrough plus the caller overlay (forwarded end-to-end through the bin), so host secrets in process.env never reach Codex, Kiro, agy, grok or later adapters unless explicitly declared or passed in env.
currentProblem: Executed probe: process-runner childEnvironment spreads process.env (minus NODE_TEST_CONTEXT) and overlays env. A planted EXHARNESS_PLANTED_SECRET and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY on the parent were present in the child; PATH and HOME were also inherited; childEnvironment is not exported. BB-067 sandboxes OpenHands, not this spawn. Plan-defect probe: the first allowlist design (allowlist plus overlay only) is unimplementable as specified — the delivered bin (exharness-agent.mjs run/smoke) calls runSupervisedTask with no env, so delivered tests that hand FAKE_AGENT_SCENARIO explicitly to the bin process lose it one hop down (AT4 x2, GR3 fail), and ambient provider auth has no explicit path to the child, so a live run could never authenticate.
constraints: Allowlist inheritance only; this is not a sandbox, gVisor wrap, network policy or FS confinement (BB-067 remains OpenHands).
Caller env overlay still wins for test fixtures (FAKE_AGENT_SCENARIO) and operator-supplied variables.

Delivered bin-driven tests hand FAKE_AGENT_SCENARIO explicitly to the bin process and must keep passing unmodified: the bin forwards an explicit narrow set (FAKE_AGENT_* test-control vars plus repeated --env KEY=VALUE operator flags) into the supervisor overlay.

Each tool's auth variables must be passable explicitly: adapters declare a frozen per-tool authEnvNames passthrough and any caller overlay key is forwarded; the ambient secret environment is never forwarded wholesale, and NODE_TEST_CONTEXT is never forwarded.

No adapter or doc in this repo names per-tool auth variables, so the plan must not invent vendor auth names as delivered truth; delivered adapters declare empty sets until vendor documentation is verified.
PATH and HOME stay inherited so authenticated CLIs can resolve binaries and homedir config without reading those files from ExHarness.
Do not change Codex, Kiro or agy argv, parsers or fixtures except tests that assert child env.
Research only in this lane: no product source edits, no self-issued readiness or fabricated Jev judgment.
Every input is labeled DELIVERED_TRUTH, PLANNED_CONTRACT or RESEARCH_DESIRED_STATE; planned contracts are never described as delivered.
successCriteria: Specify an exported inherited-environment allowlist used by the process runner so spawn no longer copies process.env wholesale, while still dropping NODE_TEST_CONTEXT.

Specify that a secret present only on process.env and absent from the caller overlay and from every tool's declared auth list is missing from the child, and that overlay keys are present even when they are not on the allowlist.
Specify that PATH and HOME remain inherited when set on the parent so CLI homedir authentication keeps working.

Specify that the bin forwards FAKE_AGENT_* and --env KEY=VALUE explicitly into the supervisor overlay so the delivered AT4/GR3 bin-driven tests pass unmodified, and that a declared per-tool auth name set on the parent reaches the child.
Specify named tests, Living trust-boundary text and index exports for the allowlist and auth passthrough.
Ground the design in the executed env-allowlist probe and the plan-defect probe and produce an exact file-level plan, negative cases and executable verification for fresh Jev readiness.
